ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic sentence كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am a pupil (boy).
   B. I am a pupil (girl).
   C. How are you? (to a girl)
   D. My name is Ahmad.

2. Which Arabic word means "and upon you peace (the reply)"? (1 mark)
   A. كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟
   B. مَرْحَبًا
   C. وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ
   D. أَنَا بِخَيْرٍ

3. Which is the best answer to kayfa haaluka? (1 mark)
   A. anaa bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillaah
   B. maʿa s-salaama
   C. ismii Ahmad
   D. hal ʿindaka hafla?

4. How is the Arabic word أُسْرَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. usra
   B. ukht
   C. bint
   D. khaal

5. What does the mark shadda tell you in the word umm? (1 mark)
   A. The word is a question
   B. The letter is silent
   C. The letter mim is said twice
   D. The vowel is long

6. What does the Arabic sentence هَذَا أَبِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. My father works.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. This is my father.
   D. This is my mother.

7. Which Arabic word means "cat"? (1 mark)
   A. قِطَّةٌ
   B. طَاوِلَةٌ
   C. كُوبٌ
   D. كِتَابٌ

8. What does the word al- do at the start of an Arabic word? (1 mark)
   A. It means 'my'
   B. It means 'and'
   C. It means 'not'
   D. It means 'the'

9. Which Arabic word means "chair"? (1 mark)
   A. كُرْسِيٌّ
   B. حَدِيقَةٌ
   C. غُرْفَةٌ
   D. سَرِيرٌ

10. How is the Arabic word اِسْمَعْ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ijlis
   B. ukhruj
   C. aghmiD ʿaynayka
   D. ismaʿ

11. What does the Arabic word اُكْتُبْ (uktub) mean? (1 mark)
   A. write
   B. raise your hand
   C. come in
   D. close the door

12. Which word do you add to an instruction to make it polite? (1 mark)
   A. min fadlika
   B. ayna
   C. al-yawm
   D. yawm

13. What does the Arabic word عِيدٌ (ʿiid) mean? (1 mark)
   A. festival
   B. friend
   C. no
   D. song

14. Which Arabic sentence means "Do you have a party? (to a boy)" (1 mark)
   A. عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ سَعِيدٌ
   B. كُلَّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْرٍ
   C. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟
   D. عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ

15. Which phrase would you say to a friend on a birthday? (1 mark)
   A. kayfa haaluka?
   B. ʿiid miilaad saʿiid
   C. maʿa s-salaama
   D. ʿafwan

16. What is the sound dh in udhun like in English? (1 mark)
   A. d in 'dog'
   B. th in 'think'
   C. z in 'zebra'
   D. th in 'this'

17. Which Arabic sentence means "I smell with my nose." (1 mark)
   A. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي
   B. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي
   C. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   D. أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي

18. What is intonation? (1 mark)
   A. The number of words
   B. The size of letters
   C. The rise and fall of the voice when speaking
   D. The speed of writing

19. Which Arabic sentence means "The water is clean." (1 mark)
   A. الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ
   B. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
   C. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ
   D. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ

20. What does the Arabic word رِيحٌ (riih) mean? (1 mark)
   A. environment
   B. wind
   C. cold
   D. beautiful

21. What is the name of the Arabic letter ز? (1 mark)
   A. dhaal
   B. alif
   C. miim
   D. zaay

22. What is the special sign hamza (ء)? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of number
   B. A short stop in the throat
   C. A dot below
   D. A long vowel

23. How do you read the syllable سِ? (1 mark)
   A. laa
   B. mu
   C. tu
   D. si

24. What does the Arabic sentence جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Hello, Ahmad.
   B. My brother is small.
   C. My grandfather is old (big in age).
   D. My sister is beautiful.

25. How is the Arabic word الثُّلَاثَاءُ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ath-thulaathaa'
   B. usbuuʿ
   C. al-ithnayn
   D. al-khamiis

26. Which Arabic word means "please, go ahead"? (1 mark)
   A. لَا
   B. تَفَضَّلْ
   C. شَمْعَةٌ
   D. عِيدُ مِيلَادٍ

27. What does the Arabic word قَوِيٌّ (qawiyy) mean? (1 mark)
   A. in
   B. friend
   C. strong
   D. oranges

28. Which Arabic sentence means "I have two eyes." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا جِسْمِي
   B. جِسْمِي قَوِيٌّ
   C. لِي عَيْنَانِ
   D. لِي يَدَانِ

29. How is the Arabic word جَوٌّ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. zahra
   B. jamiil
   C. jaww
   D. ghaa'im

30. Which Arabic word means "key"? (1 mark)
   A. كُوبٌ
   B. مِفْتَاحٌ
   C. حَمَّامٌ
   D. خِزَانَةٌ

31. How is the Arabic word أَمَامَ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. fii
   B. ʿinda
   C. amaama
   D. taHta

32. What is the name of the Arabic letter ط? (1 mark)
   A. waaw
   B. Haa
   C. alif
   D. Taa

33. Which of these letters does NOT join to the letter after it? (1 mark)
   A. ر (raa)
   B. ب (baa)
   C. س (siin)
   D. ن (nuun)

34. What does the Arabic word مَطْبَخٌ (matbakh) mean? (1 mark)
   A. key
   B. bag
   C. kitchen
   D. door

35. Which style is quick and simple and used for everyday handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. Diwani
   B. Ruqʿah
   C. Thuluth
   D. Kufic

36. What does the Arabic sentence أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. My head is big.
   B. I wash my face.
   C. I clean my teeth.
   D. My hand is small.

37. Which Arabic sentence means "I clean my teeth." (1 mark)
   A. أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي
   B. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   C. أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي
   D. يَدِي صَغِيرَةٌ

38. Which Arabic word means "face"? (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسٌ
   B. وَجْهٌ
   C. لِسَانٌ
   D. أُذُنٌ

39. What does the Arabic word جَوٌّ (jaww) mean? (1 mark)
   A. wind
   B. weather
   C. rainy
   D. cloudy

40. Which sentence means 'The wind is strong'? (1 mark)
   A. al-jawwu mumtir
   B. ar-riihu qawiyya
   C. al-jawwu ghaa'im
   D. ash-shamsu haarra

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write three body parts in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

42. Write five foods or drinks in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

43. Explain what it means to read with fluency and give two tips for reading fluently. (3 marks) (3 marks)

44. Explain why poems help us when learning a language. (2 marks) (2 marks)

45. Explain what makes a paragraph coherent. (2 marks) (2 marks)

46. Explain why neat and legible writing matters when a poem is displayed. (3 marks) (3 marks)

47. Translate into English: usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt. (2 marks) (2 marks)

48. Translate into English: nahnu narqusu (2 marks)

49. Translate into English: al-maa'u nadhiif (2 marks)

50. List four characteristics of good handwriting. (4 marks) (4 marks)

51. List the six Arabic letters that do not join to the letter that follows them. (3 marks) (3 marks)

52. Translate into English: aktubu bi-yadii (2 marks)

53. Write two describing words in Arabic sounds with their meanings, one for a masculine and one for a feminine item. (3 marks) (3 marks)

54. Sort these words into items and position words: kitaab, ʿalaa, taawila, taHta. (4 marks) (4 marks)

55. Translate into English: hadiyya li-Aminata (2 marks)

56. Translate into English: haadhihi hafla (2 marks)

57. Translate into English: ashummu bi-anfii (2 marks)

58. Name the four marks (harakat) that show short vowels or no vowel and say what each one shows. (4 marks) (4 marks)

59. Translate into English: aktubu bi-yadii. asmaʿu bi-udhunii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

60. Translate into English: fii l-matbakhi taawila wa kursii (2 marks)

61. Write the Arabic greeting for 'peace be upon you' in English letters and give the reply. (2 marks) (2 marks)

62. Translate into English: ummii tatbukhu (2 marks)

63. Translate into English: al-jawwu ghaa'im (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — How are you? (to a girl)
   كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ (kayfa haaluki?) means: How are you? (to a girl)

2. C — وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ
   وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ (wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam) means and upon you peace (the reply).

3. A — anaa bi-khayr, al-hamdu lillaah
   The question asks how you are, so the answer says 'I am well, thanks be to God'.

4. A — usra
   أُسْرَةٌ is read usra and means family.

5. C — The letter mim is said twice
   A shadda doubles the sound of a letter, so we say um-m.

6. C — This is my father.
   هَذَا أَبِي (haadhaa abii) means: This is my father.

7. A — قِطَّةٌ
   قِطَّةٌ (qitta) means cat.

8. D — It means 'the'
   al- is the word for 'the', as in al-kitaab, the book.

9. A — كُرْسِيٌّ
   كُرْسِيٌّ (kursii) means chair.

10. D — ismaʿ
   اِسْمَعْ is read ismaʿ and means listen.

11. A — write
   اُكْتُبْ (uktub) means write.

12. A — min fadlika
   min fadlika means 'please'.

13. A — festival
   عِيدٌ (ʿiid) means festival.

14. C — هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟
   هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ (hal ʿindaka hafla?) means: Do you have a party? (to a boy)

15. B — ʿiid miilaad saʿiid
   ʿiid miilaad saʿiid means 'Happy birthday'.

16. D — th in 'this'
   The letter dh is like the th in 'this'.

17. C — أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي (ashummu bi-anfii) means: I smell with my nose.

18. C — The rise and fall of the voice when speaking
   Intonation is how the voice goes up and down.

19. A — الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ
   الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ (al-maa'u nadhiif) means: The water is clean.

20. B — wind
   رِيحٌ (riih) means wind.

21. D — zaay
   The letter ز is called zaay.

22. B — A short stop in the throat
   The hamza is a short pause made in the throat, like the stop in 'uh-oh'.

23. D — si
   سِ is read si.

24. C — My grandfather is old (big in age).
   جَدِّي كَبِيرٌ (jaddii kabiir) means: My grandfather is old (big in age).

25. A — ath-thulaathaa'
   الثُّلَاثَاءُ is read ath-thulaathaa' and means Tuesday.

26. B — تَفَضَّلْ
   تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) means please, go ahead.

27. C — strong
   قَوِيٌّ (qawiyy) means strong.

28. C — لِي عَيْنَانِ
   لِي عَيْنَانِ (lii ʿaynaani) means: I have two eyes.

29. C — jaww
   جَوٌّ is read jaww and means weather.

30. B — مِفْتَاحٌ
   مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) means key.

31. C — amaama
   أَمَامَ is read amaama and means in front of.

32. D — Taa
   The letter ط is called Taa.

33. A — ر (raa)
   raa joins only to the letter before it. So do alif, daal, dhaal, zaay and waaw.

34. C — kitchen
   مَطْبَخٌ (matbakh) means kitchen.

35. B — Ruqʿah
   Ruqʿah is a short, quick style used in notes and everyday writing.

36. B — I wash my face.
   أَغْسِلُ وَجْهِي (aghsilu wajhii) means: I wash my face.

37. C — أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي
   أُنَظِّفُ أَسْنَانِي (unadhdhifu asnaanii) means: I clean my teeth.

38. B — وَجْهٌ
   وَجْهٌ (wajh) means face.

39. B — weather
   جَوٌّ (jaww) means weather.

40. B — ar-riihu qawiyya
   riih is wind and qawiyya is the feminine form of strong.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), yad (hand), fam (mouth).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example khubz (bread), aruzz (rice), dhura (maize), lahm (meat), samak (fish).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fluency means reading smoothly at a steady speed with correct words. Tips: put a finger under each word; practise at slow and normal speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for each tip.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: The rhythm and rhyme help us to remember words and to practise pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for memory and 1 mark for pronunciation.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sentences are about one topic and are in a good order, so they fit together and make sense.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for one topic and 1 mark for a logical order.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Readers can read it easily, the dots and marks show the right words, and neat work shows care and pride.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: I help my mother on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'I help my mother' and 1 mark for 'on Saturday'.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: We dance.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: The water is clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Correct letter shapes; letters the same size; letters on the baseline; correct dots and marks; even spacing; clean page.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid characteristic, up to 4.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: alif, daal, dhaal, raa, zaay and waaw.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six; 2 marks for four or five; 1 mark for two or three.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: I write with my hand.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: kabiir (big) for a masculine word and kabiira (big) for a feminine word.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each form and 1 mark for the meaning.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Items: kitaab (book), taawila (table). Position words: ʿalaa (on), taHta (under).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word placed correctly.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: A gift for Amina.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is a party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: I smell with my nose.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: fatHa gives a, kasra gives i, Damma gives u, and sukuun shows no vowel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each mark and its meaning.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: I write with my hand. I hear with my ear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sentence.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: In the kitchen there is a table and a chair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: as-salaamu ʿalaykum. The reply is wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the greeting and 1 mark for the correct reply.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: My mother cooks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

63. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is cloudy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.
